_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: System Problem Report - SPR
summary: The System Problem Report (SPR) identifies and reports hardware, software, and documentation anomalies prohibiting equipment from performing as specified during TPS development.
use_relationship:
This Data Item Description (DID) identifies anomalies prohibiting equipment from performing as specified. The anomaly can be related to hardware and software performance and documentation. This report will provide technical information to report anomalies for equipment.
This DID is applicable for use during all test program set (TPS) development program phases (design, integration, acceptance testing, and production).
This Data Item Description (DID) contains the format, content, and intended use information for the data deliverable resulting from the work task described in the contract.
This DID supersedes DI-MGMT-81232.
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Format.
preparation_instructions.content: Figure 1 provides a sample SPR format.

children.title: General.
children.content: The reports shall be written, single-spaced on one side only, single column, flush left, on good grade commercial white bond paper, 8 1/2 inches (width) by 11 inches (length) and 17 inches (width) by 11 inches (length) for foldouts. All pages of the report shall be of such legibility and contrast that every line, number, letter, and character is clear and readable. The left margin shall be wide enough so the test will not be obscured when the report is bound. Pages shall be sequentially numbered. All attachments shall be identified and referenced in the text of the report.

children.title: Binding.
children.content: The reports shall be bound in the most economical manner unless otherwise stated on DD Form 1423, Contract Data Requirement List (CDRL).

children.title: Foldout Illustrations.
children.content: Foldout illustrations should be avoided. However, if a foldout is necessary, the foldout shall not exceed 17 inches (width) by 11 inches (length).

preparation_instructions.title: Content.
preparation_instructions.content: The SPR shall include the following:

children.title: SPR Number.
children.content:
The SPR number shall include the following:
XXXXX-YYYYY-ZZZZ
XXXXX: Up to five alphabetic characters representing the reporting activity.
YYYYY: Five alphanumeric characters representing the ATE and configuration letters.
ZZZZ: Sequential four digit numeral control number (leading zeros as necessary).

children.title: Contractor.
children.content: Identify the company or agency reporting the anomaly.

children.title: Date.
children.content: Enter the date of the report.

children.title: Prepared Under Contract Number.
children.content: Enter the contract number under which the anomaly is being reported by inserting the statement "Prepared under Contract Number #####-##-#-###."

children.title: Problem Title.
children.content: Enter a brief descriptive title of the anomaly.

children.title: Priority.
children.content: Include the conditions that impair schedule performance.

children.title: Priority 01:
children.content: The anomaly has created a work stoppage situation. Work cannot proceed and scheduled events lapse. A workaround is not possible.

children.title: Priority 02:
children.content: The anomaly, if not acted upon, will affect projected work schedule. Indicate when priority will change to Priority 1 if not corrected. A workaround may be possible, but will not affect schedule.

children.title: Priority 03:
children.content: The anomaly exists, but does not affect work schedule. A workaround is possible to correct the deficiency and does not affect schedule.

children.title: TPS Affected.
children.content: Enter the TPS affected by the anomaly. Use a separate report for each TPS affected.

children.title: Problem Relation.
children.content: Enter the general category the anomaly has effected (hardware, software, documentation).

children.title: Hardware.
children.content: Enter effected hardware model number, part number, and serial number and reference designator, if applicable.

children.title: Software.
children.content: Enter effected software, operating system, test executive, compiler, or post processor, as applicable. Include version number and date.

children.title: Documentation.
children.content: Enter the effected volume, book, chapter, page, paragraph, table, and figure, as applicable.

children.title: Problem Description.
children.content: Include schedule impact statement here. Include all substantial evidence describing the anomaly. Include, as applicable, program listings, print outs, figures, illustrations, and tables. Indicate, if a demonstration is required to manifest the anomaly.

children.title: Action Taken/Recommended Workaround.
children.content: Include all programming techniques required to work around the anomaly. Indicate if the workaround will be a permanent "fix" for the TPS or will be required to be removed prior to acceptance testing once the anomaly is resolved.

children.title: Point of Contact.
children.content: Include a point of contact in the event additional information is required.
